vars.team_intro: For significant features or changes that are more than a few lines of code, run a team of Codex subagents with a structured multi-agent approach. You are the lead: spawn each role with `spawn_agent` using its agent type, leave `fork_context` off so every role starts with only the prompt you give it, and use `wait_agent` to finish a phase before starting the next.
vars.guard_hooks: A `PreToolUse` hook blocks subagents other than the tester from `apply_patch` edits to sealed files, and a `SubagentStop` hook sends a subagent back to work while a sealed test is modified.
vars.worktree_section: **All agents must work in the same worktree directory.** Before spawning any agent, set up a single worktree for the feature branch (`git worktree add`) and start Codex from inside it, so every subagent inherits it as its working directory.
vars.phase_intro:
### Phased execution

Codex has no task dependencies, so you enforce phase ordering as the lead. Agents within a phase can run in parallel; don't spawn the next phase until every agent in the current one has finished and you've checked its output.
vars.ask_tester: stop and report to the lead, who relays it to the tester,
vars.goal_mechanics: Codex attaches the goal to the active chat as a persistent objective (`/goal` shows it; `/goal pause`, `resume`, `edit`, and `clear` manage it), and `max_goal_token_budget` in `config.toml` caps its spend. Codex's docs don't say whether it starts new turns on its own; if it waits after a turn, send `continue` or resume the goal.
